Framing and gesture: confirmed correct across all seeds — clean waist_up crop, fully symmetric raised-hand gesture at chest/hip height, centered on the frame.

Camera elevation: the original hold's core observation still holds at full resolution — the background is a plain seamless gradient with zero floor line, wall seam, or any perspective geometry in any of the three seeds, so there is no environmental cue to confirm or deny an elevated camera. I additionally checked facial geometry (the usual tell for a high-angle shot: enlarged forehead/crown, shortened chin, upward-directed eye gaze/sclera). None of the three seeds show these tells — the gaze is level and direct, proportions look like a standard eye-line portrait, not an obviously elevated one.

So the pipeline may simply render 'slight' elevation too subtly to read on a plain-background headshot-style crop by design, the same way airy_pastel legitimately reads near 0.10 saturation. There is no contradicting evidence either (e.g., a clearly low-angle or tilted-back look) — just an absence of confirming cues, in all three seeds alike, at full resolution.

Since higher resolution doesn't add any perspective information that was missing at thumbnail size (the limitation is compositional — no floor/lines exist in the source image at any resolution — not a compression/thumbnail artifact of legibility), and there is no actual visible defect (wrong angle, broken geometry, or clear failure to elevate) once inspected closely, this is not a genuine confirmed defect. It resolves as a case that should be released from hold rather than failed: the concern was an inherent unconfirmability of a subtle camera tag on a plain-background crop, not a rendering fault.
